title: Orca 502 debug log + comms draft
content:
Top-level: scratchpad for the Orca (customer) 502 spikes observed on 2025-11-03 through 2025-11-06. This is a personal notes / comms draft doc — messy, steps tried, raw errors, and a short customer-facing note draft. DO NOT SHARE AS-IS.

TL;DR: Orca reported intermittent 502s from hosted API (edge -> proxy -> runtime). Errors cluster around high-concurrency rps and long context lengths (~12k tokens). Hypothesis: a combination of KV cache OOMs and grpc message size / proxy timeout miscoordination.

Timeline (rough):
- 2025-11-03 09:12 PST: first customer alert (Slack DM from Orca SE). Report: some requests returned 502, ~0.5% of requests during load test.
- 2025-11-03 09:19 PST: I reproduced locally with script that mimics Orca prompt shape (long prompt + streaming).
- 2025-11-03 09:25 PST: Escalated to SRE; opened JIRA-7894.
- 2025-11-03 10:05 PST: Observed increase in proxy 502 logs synchronized with runtime logs showing \"E [2025-11-03T09:22:11Z] KV cache allocation failed: requested 32768 KB, available 8192 KB\" on instance r-34.
- 2025-11-04 02:20 PST: Canary rollback to q8 quantized variant reduced error rate but did not eliminate it.
- 2025-11-05 16:40 PST: Deployed temporary increase of grpc/max_msg_size and proxy timeout to 90s for the Orca tenant. Error rate dropped to ~0.05% during afternoon load.
- 2025-11-06 11:10 PST: Root cause still unclear; follow-ups scheduled.

Commands & snippets tried (raw):
1) Reproduce load (local):
- python tools/loadgen.py --host api.redwood-hosted.example --model rwd-instruct-v1 --concurrency 40 --prompt-file orca-long-prompts.json --stream True

2) Instance logs (via gcloud/ssh):
- kubectl logs -n runtime r-34 -c runtime --since=1h | grep -i error
  -> got repeated lines: \"E [2025-11-03T09:22:11Z] KV cache allocation failed: requested 32768 KB, available 8192 KB\"

3) Proxy logs (nginx):
- tail -n 200 /var/log/nginx/proxy_access.log | grep 502
- cat /var/log/nginx/proxy_error.log | tail -n 200
  -> snippets: \"2025/11/03 09:22:12 [error] 1234#0: *765 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.1.4.8, server: api.redwood-hosted.example\"

4) Debugging grpc boundary:
- tcpdump -i eth0 port 50051 -w /tmp/grpc-orca.pcap (ran for short window)
- grpc-gateway logs show \"rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = bytes limit exceeded\" on same timeframe

5) Heap/host health (r-34):
- top, free -h: memory pressure spike at same time (swap used briefly)
- dmesg: \"Out of memory: Kill process 2311 (runtime) total-vm: 1200000kB...\" (but no oom_kill in kube events)

Quick findings:
- Runtime instance r-34 reported KV cache allocation failures and later restarted worker threads. These correlate tightly with the 502 window.
- Proxy 502s are upstream-closed (upstream crashed / connection closed); likely the runtime closed connection mid-request.
- grpc error messages included \"bytes limit exceeded\" suggesting either the server is rejecting large response frames or an intermediary limit.
- Increasing max_msg_size on the runtime grpc server and proxy allowed longer responses but only reduced error rate, didn't remove failures (still see rare OOM).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Primary: KV cache growth with long contexts + concurrency triggers memory pressure leading to worker crashes/connection closes. When runtime rapidly tries to allocate for prefix cache it fails and closes connection -> proxy sees upstream closed -> 502.
2) Secondary: grpc message size threshold mismatch between runtime / proxy / client; some long streamed messages exceed configured max sizes causing immediate rpc failures.
3) Tertiary: scheduling/allocation bug in serving runtime kernel selection under quantized variant causing rare crash under specific token shapes.

Immediate mitigation steps taken: 
- throttled Orca tenant concurrency from 40 -> 16 for one hour (reduced observed errors).
- temporarily increased runtime KV cache hard limit for the Orca pool (risky) and added metric alarms.
- bumped grpc max_msg_size and proxy buffer to 10MB for Orca routes.

Next actions (private notes):
- [ ] Capture heap dump / jemalloc stats from r-34 on next repro (low-latency window) -> may require scheduled repro window and live capture script.
- [ ] Add instrumentation to record per-request kv-cache delta and response frame size in tracing (small PR).
- [ ] Run longer stress test with headroom (50% higher) to validate stability and reproduce OOM.
- [ ] Try running same workload on dedicated node-type with extra memory to see if OOM goes away (helps confirm memory constraint vs bug).
- [ ] If confirmed memory pressure, propose config change: per-tenant kv-cache quota + admission control for long-context requests (opt-in).

Notes for customer comms (DRAFT):
- Slack / email short: \"Hi <Orca contact>, we investigated the 502s you saw on Nov 3-5. Root cause appears related to large-context requests under high concurrency triggering memory pressure on our runtime which caused some requests to be closed mid-flight. We've applied temporary mitigations (reduced concurrency, increased grpc buffers) and are rolling out further fixes. We will follow up with a postmortem and longer-term fix (per-tenant cache quotas + tracing). Apologies for the disruption — appreciate your patience.\"

- Longer internal-to-customer post (for review):
  Subject: Update: 502 errors during high-concurrency long-context runs (Nov 3-6)
  Body draft: \"Summary: From Nov 3-6, a small fraction of your requests returned 502. We traced this to memory pressure inside the inference runtime when serving long prompts concurrently. Impact: ~0.3-0.5% of requests during peak load; no data loss. Mitigation: reduced concurrency, temporary buffer increases, and instance restarts. Planned fix: per-tenant resource quotas, improved tracing, and a robust admission control for very long-context requests. ETA for full rollout: 3 weeks pending validation.\"

Messaging notes: be explicit about impact (percent/time), avoid deep internals. Offer workaround: throttle, reduce max tokens, or use dedicated capacity.

Misc raw snippets to preserve (for postmortem):
- runtime error lines: \"E 2025-11-03T09:22:11Z runtime::kv_cache.cpp: failed alloc(32768): returned null\"
- grpc error: \"rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = bytes limit exceeded\"
- proxy: \"upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header\"

Questions / unknowns to resolve:
- Why did kube not show oom_kill events even though dmesg recorded OOM? Investigate container runtime vs host-level OOM handling.
- Are there specific prompt shapes (tokens with lots of embeddings) that cause cache blowup? Need per-token shape stats.
- Could the quantized kernel path allocate transiently larger working memory leading to spikes? Check kernel selection traces.

Quick dev notes for tomorrow:
- Start with reproducer that increases token length slowly; run with pprof attached.
- Add a 1s sleep in runtime before streaming first frame (debug) to see if proxy timeouts are a factor.

References / links to add into final PM: JIRA-7894, github PR 1123 (kv-cache metrics), slack thread #orca-prod (pinned).

One-line internal summary (for pager duty / huddles):
- \"Orca 502s: memory pressure from kv-cache during long-context, high-concurrency runs causing upstream closures; temporary mitigations in place; collecting dumps + adding per-request cache metrics next.\"

End of scratchpad.

-- evan
